basis: Defining keratoderma/hypohidrosis, enamel defects and intellectual disability; hepatitis is occasional; respiratory infections do not establish immunodeficiency.
Congenital viral infection with defining destructive brain abnormalities and retinal/optic nerve lesions; hearing loss and contractures are less common.
Primary gastric malignancy; liver metastases directly occupy hepatic tissue in roughly 50-70% of reported cases; pulmonary metastases are less consistently above 30%.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, persistent ptosis and metopic/craniosynostosis abnormalities define the syndrome; hearing impairment and cardiac defects are occasional.
Ear, eye and cranial nerve/developmental defects define CHARGE; hypogonadotropic hypogonadism occurs in 80-99%. Common choanal and cardiac defects omitted under the four-axis cap.
Exocrine pancreatic primary; hepatic metastases directly occupy liver in approximately half or more over the disease course.
Hereditary recurrent dysfunction of the peripheral facial nerve; facial muscle weakness reflects neuropathy.
Malignant precursor T-cell disease involving blood/marrow or lymphoid tissue; lymphoma warrants the immune mechanism axis.
Adhesive inflammation and fibrosis of spinal arachnoid injure nerve roots/spinal cord; infection or autoimmunity is not intrinsic to all cases.
Chronic immune-mediated mast-cell disease of skin; individual wheals are transient but recurrent cutaneous disease defines the condition.
Acute malignant myeloid blood/marrow disease defined by its chromosomal translocation; no established common additional organ injury.
Adult Leigh disease is mitochondrial metabolic encephalomyelopathy; supplied periosteal/skin HPO findings are discordant with this diagnosis.
Primary brain sarcoma; myogenic or chondroid differentiation does not establish disease in skeletal muscle or bone.
Disordered calcium handling with excessive urinary calcium defines this urinary/metabolic disorder; increased intestinal absorption does not imply intestinal injury.
Biotin metabolic defect; seizures/developmental impairment and persistent dermatitis/alopecia each affect roughly 30% or more of symptomatic patients across the main forms.
Complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy defined by hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and kidney injury; hypertension usually accompanies renal injury.
Deficiency or dysfunction of coagulation proteins; no particular additional organ sustains direct injury in most patients across this umbrella.
Smoldering plasma-cell neoplasm lacks myeloma-defining end-organ damage; bone lesions and renal injury must not be inferred from active myeloma.
Inherited complement immunodeficiency; meningococcal infection is a separately diagnosed consequence, not intrinsic neurologic damage from properdin deficiency.
Inherited susceptibility specifically concerns cutaneous melanoma; no current tumor or additional organ injury is inferred from susceptibility alone.
Dilatation of renal collecting structures from impaired urine drainage; associated nausea or fever does not establish other organ injury.
Pure anxiety disorder; muscle tension, concentration difficulty and sleep disturbance do not establish damage to an organ axis.
Disease of myocardium of unknown cause; neither immune disease nor skeletal muscle involvement applies across the umbrella.
Progressive brain degeneration; fixed flexion contractures occur in 30-79% and cause lasting joint restriction. Incontinence reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Broad category of sequelae attributable to viral infection; affected anatomical organs vary by subtype, with no shared organ damage established across the umbrella.
